newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan, Red Cross hold talks on grounded aid plane.
newsitem.headline: Sudan, Red Cross hold talks on grounded aid plane.

text.p: An official was quoted on Sunday as saying Sudan and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) were trying to resolve a dispute in which Sudan halted the group's activities and detained some of its workers.

The Sudanese government last Tuesday suspended all ICRC work, saying one of its planes was carrying arms and troops loyal to the rebel Sudan People Liberation Army (SPLA) headed by Colonel John Garang.
For 13 years, the SPLA has been fighting for the autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south from Sudan's Islamist dominated north.

A state-owned newspaper quoted Minister of State in the Foreign Ministry Mustafa Osman Ismail as saying his government and the ICRC had agreed "to work to resolve the issue (the grounded plane) in a way that prevents a recurrence of the incident".
It did not give any details.
A pro-government group seized the ICRC plane, which flew from northern Kenya to Wunruk in Sudan's Bahr el-Ghazal province.

A Red Cross spokesman in Nairobi said envoy Paul Grossreider was in Khartoum seeking the release of the plane's two pilots, a nurse and five Sudanese patients. He said they were still being held, but were well.
He said ICRC operations in Sudan would remain suspended until the plane was freed.
